newsitem.title: USA: Groups complain to Gore on yield burning progress.
newsitem.headline: Groups complain to Gore on yield burning progress.

text.p: Top muni groups told Vice President Al Gore this week they are exasperated with the administration's lack of input on how it plans to proceed on yield burning, a spokesman said Thursday.

Frank Shafroth, director of federal relations for the National League of Cities, said groups wrote Gore Wednesday that the Internal Revenue Service still has not published a final yield burning standard even though Gore promised groups in a June meeting that the standards were imminent.

Yield burning refers to allegations that bond underwriters overcharged states and localities in recent years for U.S. Treasury securities purchased in the open market to help refinance outstanding bonds.
In July 1996, IRS announced that municipalities can avoid having bonds declared taxable by settling any overcharges with the agency now.

Following heavy criticism from muni groups, IRS scrubbed the notice's one-year deadline for issuers to enter into voluntary agreements with IRS. It also requested comment on the issue. But it did not change the bulk of the offer.
Muni groups want Gore to push IRS and the Securities and Exchange Commission to work cooperatively on resolving the yield burning problem.
They want IRS to relax its position that issuers pay for arbitrage problems -- if the SEC can collect lost federal dollars through enforcement actions.
Shafroth told Reuters that Wednesday's letter reminds Gore of three things he told muni groups at the June meeting.

Gore told them that a final IRS notice is imminent, that the final plan will incorporate the views of states and localities, and that Treasury and SEC have stated publicly that they are coordinating their efforts, according to Shafroth.
Shafroth contended that SEC and IRS have not stated formally that they are coordinating efforts on yield burning.
A spokesman for Gore was not available. Shafroth did not make the groups' letter to the vice president available.

The seven groups, dubbed the Group of Seven, include the League, U.S. Conference of Mayors, National Governors' Association, Council of State Governments, National Council of State Legislatures, International City-County Management Association, and the National Association of Counties.
